newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.8 pct at 337.33.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.8 pct at 337.33.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.8 percent to 337.33 by midsession on Wednesday.
Latin America rose 1.3 percent day-on-day to 646.49, Asia was up 0.5 percent at 269.74 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.9 percent at 164.26.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars, was up 1.69 percent day-on-day at 181.82 at 1215 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.61 percent at 537.206, calculated after the close of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.02 percent to 127.59 by the start of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America and Asia were flat at 107.19 and 133.22 respectively, while East Europe was up 0.01 percent at 160.32. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
